symptom: Under `run --local --watch`, after roughly ten hot-applies a page dies with the runtime's generic error dialog and `runtime.log` fills with `404 - file not found for file: dist%2Fchunks%2F<hash>.js`. The model is clean, `mx check` is clean, and a plain restart fixes it with no model change
cause: The browser bundle is internally inconsistent: `index.js` imports a content-hashed chunk that is not on disk. `ensureClientServed` probes **only `/dist/index.js`**, which is served with a 200 in this state — so the apply is reported as successful and the fault reads as an application bug
insight: **Walk the import graph from `index.js`, and follow only chunks that EXIST.** An orphan left by an earlier bundle references old hashes, so scanning every file in `chunks/` reports a healthy bundle as broken. One level is not enough either — a real rollup bundle has `index.js` importing a single chunk with the rest hanging off it, so a one-level check misses almost every real breakage. The safety control matters more than the detection here, because this gates an automatic re-bundle: run it against several REAL built bundles and require zero findings, then delete one referenced chunk from a copy and require detection. ako/mxcli-maintenance-2
